units.title: Lecture 1 - Ambulation & Transfer
units.summary: HHS4867 Functional Movement Science Ambulation & Transfer Learning Objectives By the end of this lecture, students will be able to understand and to perform: Bed mobility & Transfer activities Assisting ambulation with aids Bed mobility Mobility activities are used to adjust recumbent patient’s body position, they may be performed: - Independently by patient - With assistance from other person - By use of various type of equipment ⚫ Common types of bed mobility: - Bridging - Moving across the bed (supine) - Upward / downward movement (supine) - Supine to side-lying Bridging (both leg or single leg) 1. Patient assumes crook lying position with the elbow flexed to about 90°°, feet flat on bed 2. Patient presses down firmly with the elbows and head 3. Patient arches his back and push down with the lower limb(s), raises the pelvis slightly clear of the supporting surface 3.1. Assists patient by lifting his pelvis up with both hands Moving across the bed 1.
